title: OpenAI posted 722 AI-written math papers. Now someone has to check them.

say: OpenAI just dropped 722 math manuscripts on GitHub.
Every one came from an AI model the public can't use.
The model was given about 4,000 problems.
It produced 722 manuscripts, in 372 families of results.
Careful: those are different units. They don't add up to a success rate.
The claims are big: the four-dimensional Kakeya conjecture, and work touching the Riemann and Hodge conjectures.
But the Riemann result is a weaker version. It doesn't solve the famous problem.
Many come with proofs checked by Lean, a proof assistant.
One count found 162 manuscripts with formalized main results. That's 22.4 percent.
And a machine-checked proof isn't automatically a meaningful one.
These are preprints, not peer-reviewed papers.
The proofs are public. The model isn't.
Now it's up to mathematicians to check the work.

ticker: 722 MANUSCRIPTS — 372 FAMILIES — 162 FORMALIZED — NOW CHECK THE WORK
